Roadmap

Roadmap and gap register

What is done, what is next, the gaps the audit found, and the lessons planned to close them.

Each phase has an exit gate. A phase is not finished until its gate is met.

Planned lessons

13 lessons, each with a lab and an artefact for the portfolio.

  • P1Model pipelines: data, training, registry and signing Planned Level 2 · AISVS C1, C3, C6
    Closes the GAIPS development-pipelines and MLOps cluster: data lineage, training and fine-tuning pipelines, CI/CD, model registry, artefact signing, evaluation gates and rollback.
  • P2Fine-tuning, adapters and alignment: poisoning, backdoors and limits Planned Level 2 · AISVS C1, C3, C7, C11
    Closes the model customisation and alignment cluster: dataset lineage, backdoor and poisoning risk, safety regression, and why alignment is not a security boundary.
  • P3Inference, serving and AI infrastructure hardening Planned Level 3 · AISVS C4
    Hardened inference and deployment environments, isolation, secrets, network controls, runtime policy and cloud shared responsibility, taught at configuration level.
  • P4Privacy, sensitive data and logging in agent systems Planned Level 2 · AISVS C8; UK and EU data-protection principles
    Prompt and log retention, leakage, minimisation, deletion, training reuse, residency and access control as data moves between tools, providers, logs and retrieval stores.
  • P5Agent action safety: approvals, previews and emergency stop Planned Level 3 · ASI08, ASI09; AISVS C9
    Transaction previews, approval integrity, dual control, irreversible-action limits and bounded autonomy, so a successful injection cannot become an incident.
  • P6Multi-agent failure and cascade testing Planned Level 3 · ASI07, ASI08, ASI10
    Delegation loops, trust propagation, shared memory, correlated failure, recursive tool calls, cost exhaustion and cascading action, with tests that expose them.
  • P7Agent-to-agent protocols: discovery, authentication and replay Planned Level 3 · ASI07; AISVS C9, C10
    Protocol security beyond MCP: discovery, authentication, authorisation, message integrity, replay, versioning and provenance of agents and servers.
  • P8Detection engineering with MITRE ATLAS Planned Level 4 · AISVS C12; MITRE ATLAS
    Turning agent traces into detections and response playbooks, including the MITRE OpenClaw case studies as worked examples.
  • P9Foundations bridge: networks, operating systems, cloud and cryptography Planned Level 1 · Level 1 modules 3 and 4
    A short bridge for learners who arrive without networking, operating-systems or cryptography fundamentals, so Level 1 does not assume them.
  • P10Sector safety and operational technology boundaries Planned Level 6 · ASI08, ASI09
    Safety engineering, human factors, OT boundaries and service continuity, so a security control cannot create an unsafe condition.
  • P11The Secure Agentic Enterprise Dossier: building the portfolio Planned Level 1 · All levels
    The single evolving portfolio the academy uses as evidence: templates, validation, versioning and export, introduced at Level 1 and extended at every level.
  • P13Mapping agent controls to NIST: CSF, Cyber AI Profile and SP 800-53 overlays Planned Level 3 · NIST CSF 2.0; Cyber AI Profile; SP 800-53 overlays
    Architects and governance leads must express agent controls in the language auditors already use. Maps the academy control matrix to NIST CSF 2.0, the Cyber AI Profile and the SP 800-53 overlays for AI as they are finalised.
  • P12External exam orientation: published objectives and exam mechanics Planned Level 2 · GAIPS public objectives
    Familiarisation with the public objectives and format of external exams, using original practice items only. Kept separate from Intellica assessment.

How releases work

  • Each release is a checkpoint with a changelog, a test run and a review date.
  • Existing course addresses, paid access and learner progress are never changed by an academy release.
  • Academy pages never state a price, a credential or a result that the course and its tests do not already support.

Reviewed 2026-11-24. Intellica is independent of GIAC, ISC2, ISACA, CompTIA, CSA, IAPP, OWASP, MITRE and NIST. Mappings show how our lessons relate to published objectives. They are not an affiliation, an approval or a prediction of any exam result.
